record.summary: The central bank's own CV for its General Manager lists his bank roles (International Operations Manager 1994-1996, General Manager 1996-2006 and General Manager again from 16 January 2020) and names three financial employers: Banco de la Unión S.A., Banco de Cochabamba and Compañía Boliviana de Seguros S.A., with no dates. Ownership: not stated by any source opened. Searches of the Bolivian insurance and financial registers (ASFI and the pensions and insurance authority) returned no page stating who owns Compañía Boliviana de Seguros, and the CV itself says nothing about the ownership of any of the three employers.
record.status: career move, no finding; ownership of the employers unsettled

record.summary: Curaçao Chronicle reports that a person recently appointed chief executive of a commercial bank had until recently been a Director at the central bank, that the formal resignation was submitted on 26 June 2025 and the new position began on 1 July 2025, and that CBCS had taken decisions on the matter as early as 1 December 2024. The report states that the new employer operates under the direct supervisory authority of the central bank, and that no mention was made of the specific commercial bank name. Ownership: not stated by any source opened - the report calls the employer a commercial bank but never says it is privately owned, and it does not name the bank.

record.kind: statutory arrangement letting the government order an investigation of the bank
record.summary: Section 66(2) of the Bank of Namibia Act, 2020 (Act 1 of 2020) lets the Minister, on reasonable grounds, direct the Auditor-General to investigate and report on the Bank's accounts or affairs, and obliges the Bank to give the Auditor-General the information and facilities requested. Section 66(3) requires the Auditor-General's report to follow the Minister's directives and to be submitted to the Minister. The same Act, at section 5, says the Bank must act without direction from any person or authority and makes interference with its independence an offence.
record.source_title: Bank of Namibia Act 1 of 2020 (Namibia Legal Information Institute)
record.quote: the Minister may, if there are reasonable grounds to do so, direct that the Auditor-General investigate
